evidence.detail: rs/k frame loading constructs one rs/K definition and assigns that same object to every decoded frame; rs/K supplies the transform-type array and label-group arrays used while each frame's sparse transforms are decoded.
Model animation application reads rs.K transform types and label groups, then applies each frame's X/Y/Z values to the referenced vertex/face groups.
rs/K is primarily an int[] transform-type table plus int[][] label groups, with optional extended skeletal metadata; it contains no per-frame transform values.

proposals.note: Skeleton is the conservative modern semantic name for the shared transform-definition / label-group object. It is not a claim that the original developer used this exact identifier.

evidence.detail: Each rs/k instance stores one rs/K definition, a transform count, transform-index array and parallel X/Y/Z transform arrays.
The rs/k loader decodes sparse transform flags, injects default transforms when required by the shared definition, and stores per-transform X/Y/Z values for one frame id.
Model resolves rs/k by sequence/frame id and applies its transforms by indexing the attached rs/K definition, including blended-frame paths.

proposals.note: AnimationFrame is the conservative semantic name for one sparse transform frame bound to a Skeleton; it avoids ambiguity with SequenceDefinition and does not claim a verbatim original identifier.
